description: End-to-end QuickBooks integration covering automated invoice creation, webhook event handling using the CloudEvents specification, multi-account migration, and edge case handling for credit memos and negative line item amounts. The workflow is triggered when an invoice is created on the admin panel: a corresponding QuickBooks invoice is automatically generated (creating the customer record if absent), invoice items are mapped to the correct QB line items, and when payment is marked in QuickBooks the webhook fires to sync the payment status back internally. Migrated from a legacy QB account to a new account mid-project — a process that involved re-mapping all invoice item identifiers, re-configuring OAuth credentials, updating webhook endpoints to use CloudEvents payload format, and verifying all three invoice types (standard, credit-applied, zero-dollar) on production before go-live.
impact: Fully automated the licensing invoice creation and payment flow. Eliminated manual QuickBooks data entry by the accounts team. Integrated webhook-driven payment detection using CloudEvents. Handled financial edge cases including credit memos and zero-dollar invoices.
learnings:
QuickBooks OAuth and API integration
Webhook event handling with CloudEvents specification
Automating accounting workflows end-to-end
Handling financial edge cases in third-party systems
Production migration without downtime

description: Built an admin dashboard to view, manage, and respond to consultation requests submitted by users across various service categories. The dashboard features filtering by request type, status, and date range; pagination; status management (pending, reviewed, completed); and a detail view per request showing the user's submitted information and any admin notes or follow-up actions. The accompanying backend API was optimized to support paginated filtering across potentially large datasets without performance degradation.
impact: Centralized consultation request management for admins. Improved visibility and response time tracking. Replaced a fragmented email-based process with a structured admin interface.
learnings:
Dashboard development for business data management
Paginated API design for filtered datasets

description: Integrated Twilio SMS messaging into the platform, enabling admins to send targeted SMS notifications to users. Built an admin interface to compose messages, select recipients by filter criteria, and send. Each message is logged with delivery status tracking via Twilio's status callback webhook, providing visibility into delivered, failed, and pending messages. Implemented opt-out tracking and status display so admins can identify users who have opted out of SMS communications before sending.
impact: Enabled a direct SMS communication channel with users. Full message lifecycle tracking from send to delivery status. Opt-out compliance tracking built in.
learnings:
Twilio API and SMS integration
SMS delivery webhook handling and status tracking
Opt-out management and compliance

description: Built a system to configure, assign, and manage benefit packages tied to user subscriptions and hospital affiliations. Admins can define benefit types, set eligibility rules by plan or user type, assign benefits to users, and view active benefit assignments per user. The connect platform shows users their currently active benefit entitlements. Used as the foundation for the benefits program portal feature that surfaces benefit details to enrolled users.
impact: Streamlined benefit configuration and assignment for the operations team. Enabled user-facing benefit visibility on the connect platform.
learnings:
Benefits eligibility logic and rule-based assignment
Admin-to-user data surface design

task: Bulk License Creation — Florida Healthcare Professionals
description: Automated bulk creation of regulatory state licenses for previously bulk-registered healthcare professionals. Sourced license data from state registry exports, matched each record to the corresponding registered user by email and profession, and created license records at scale via admin-authenticated API calls. Implemented per-record validation to skip malformed or unmatched entries, with result logging to track success counts, skipped records, and errors across each run. Used across multiple bulk cohort operations following the user registration phase.
impact: Created tens of thousands of license records in automated runs, significantly reducing manual data entry for the licensing team. Established a safe, resumable bulk license creation pattern.
learnings:
Batch database operations at scale
Data matching and validation from external registry sources
Safe re-run strategies with per-record result tracking

description: Developed an admin dashboard providing a performance overview for licensing analysts, showing key operational metrics such as total licenses handled, licenses completed on time, overdue licenses, and task completion rates — filterable by analyst, date range, and license type. Includes an export capability for reporting, and a comparison view showing team-level aggregates alongside individual analyst performance. Designed to support data-driven performance reviews and workload balancing decisions.
impact: Enabled management to monitor analyst productivity and workload distribution. Supported data-driven performance reviews and workload balancing.
learnings:
Aggregated metrics dashboard design
Performance data visualization and reporting

description: Implemented functionality to fetch and download license primary source verification reports from an external license verification service (Lumexa), integrated directly into the admin licenses workflow. Admins can trigger a report download for any license from within the license detail view without leaving the admin panel. The backend proxies the request to Lumexa's API, streams the report file back to the client, and handles error states for licenses where reports are unavailable.
impact: Enabled admins to directly access external verification reports without leaving the admin panel. Eliminated manual download-and-upload workflows.
learnings:
Third-party API proxying and file streaming
Integrating external verification services into admin workflows

task: User Name Confirmation When Attempting Quiz
description: Added a mandatory pre-quiz confirmation step requiring users to verify that their profile name displayed on screen matches their legal name before beginning a quiz. If the name is incorrect, users are directed to their profile settings to update it before proceeding. This ensures that any certificates generated upon quiz completion carry the user's correct legal name, reducing post-generation support requests for name corrections.
impact: Reduced support requests related to name mismatches on generated certificates. Ensured certificate accuracy before quiz commencement.
learnings:
UX improvement for data accuracy in certification workflows
Pre-action validation patterns

description: Built a calendar view for licensing invoices, allowing admins and analysts to visualize invoice due dates, payment timelines, and status distribution on a monthly calendar grid. Each day cell shows the count and status breakdown of invoices due on that date. Clicking a cell opens a list of those invoices with quick-action links. Color-coded status indicators (due, overdue, paid) provide instant visual scanning across the month. Built using a calendar grid component integrated with the invoices API, with month navigation and filter support by license type and status.
impact: Provided a time-based view of invoice activity, improving planning and reducing missed payment follow-ups.
learnings:
Calendar-based data visualization
Invoice lifecycle management
Time-oriented dashboard design

description: Developed a comprehensive invoices management dashboard for admins, replacing a legacy list view with limited capabilities. Built a new optimized API supporting advanced filtering by invoice status, date range, license type, provider, and amount; sortable and configurable columns; pagination; CSV export; filter presets for frequent queries; and inline action buttons per row. The dashboard includes a summary metrics bar showing total invoice counts by status category at the top of the page, giving admins an at-a-glance financial overview before drilling into individual records.
impact: Significantly improved invoice data visibility and management efficiency. Replaced a slow, limited legacy interface with a performant, feature-rich dashboard. Enabled financial reporting via CSV export.
learnings:
Admin dashboard design for financial data
Advanced filtering and export systems
Summary metrics design for operational dashboards

description: Integrated the IMLC (Interstate Medical Licensure Compact) license type for physicians into the platform, allowing physicians who hold a compact license to have it tracked alongside their state-specific licenses. The IMLC compact grants practice rights across multiple member states from a single license, so the integration required custom handling for multi-state coverage display, eligibility checking, and status tracking. Changes spanned the backend API license logic, admin panel certificate and license pages, consultant registration flow, and the user-facing state license section on the connect platform. Produced a reusable integration reference document for future license type additions.
impact: Expanded license coverage for physician users. Enabled IMLC compact license tracking across all admin and user-facing interfaces.
learnings:
License type integration across multiple platform layers
Handling multi-state compact license logic
Documenting integration patterns for future scalability

description: Integrated new third-party Grassblade LMS-hosted courses into the platform, enabling users to access them through the standard course purchase and navigation flow. The integration involved configuring backend access control rules to gate course access by subscription plan type, setting up frontend course cards and navigation routing, linking course orders to the Grassblade course IDs for access validation, and verifying correct access token handoff to the Grassblade iframe on course launch.
impact: Expanded course catalog with additional specialized clinical content for users. Maintained consistent access control patterns with existing courses.
learnings:
Third-party LMS course integration workflow
Subscription-gated access control implementation

description: Built an enhanced users management dashboard for the admin panel, replacing a legacy user list with limited search and no filtering. The new dashboard supports advanced search by name, email, and profession; filtering by registration date range, account status, plan type, and hospital affiliation; sortable columns; paginated results; CSV export; and inline user actions (view, edit, suspend). Built a new optimized API to support the advanced filtering without loading the full user dataset. Handles a user base of tens of thousands of records with sub-second response times.
impact: Replaced a slow, limited user list with a performant dashboard. Significantly reduced time spent by admins locating and managing users.
learnings:
High-volume user data management with optimized filtering APIs
Admin dashboard UX optimization

description: Developed an enhanced admin dashboard for viewing individual user course progress in detail, replacing a legacy progress page with limited data visibility and no export capability. Built a new optimized API with advanced filtering by user, course, date range, and progress status. The dashboard displays initial access date, latest access date, completion percentage, quiz attempt status, and pass/fail for each course per user. Supports column management, Excel export for reporting, and pagination for large datasets. The legacy page had slow API response times and displayed LMS progress data that was confusing and irrelevant to the actual in-platform progress tracking.
impact: Significantly improved user course progress visibility for admins. Enabled Excel export for reporting. Added course initial and latest access date tracking. Replaced a slow, confusing legacy page.
learnings:
Optimized admin view design for user-course progress data
Multi-dimensional filtering for user and course data
Excel export integration in admin dashboards

description: Integrated the FCVS (Federation Credentials Verification Service) license type into the platform. FCVS is a credentialing intermediary that collects and verifies physician credentials on behalf of licensing authorities, so the integration required a distinct license handling flow from standard state licenses. Changes spanned: backend API logic for FCVS-specific validation and status handling, admin panel certificate management pages, the consultant registration flow to include FCVS as a selectable license type, and the user-facing state license section on the connect platform to display FCVS license status. Documented the integration process as a reusable template for future license type additions.
impact: New FCVS license type available and trackable across all admin and user-facing interfaces. Integration documentation reduced future license onboarding time.
learnings:
Cross-platform license type integration
Handling credentialing intermediary workflows
Maintaining scalable integration documentation

task: Bulk User Registration — Florida Healthcare Professionals
description: Developed a bulk user registration automation system to onboard large cohorts of licensed healthcare professionals sourced from state license registries. State-provided CSV data was pre-converted to JSON using a custom conversion script. Each user was then registered via a secure admin-authenticated API with built-in deduplication (skip if email already exists), deceased-user exclusion, UTM parameter injection for acquisition attribution, and suppression of welcome credential emails to avoid spamming users who may already be registered. The system was designed to be idempotent — safe to re-run without creating duplicates — and was used across multiple Florida healthcare profession datasets (APRN, Physician, MD).
impact: Registered over 100,000 licensed professionals in a single automated run. Established a reusable, idempotent framework for future bulk onboarding operations.
learnings:
Large-scale data operations and batch processing
Idempotency and safe re-run design
Controlled execution for high-volume operations
Attribution tracking with UTM parameters

description: Enabled simulation case access for the PALS (Pediatric Advanced Life Support) course, building on the existing ACLS simulation infrastructure. Implemented backend access control logic that evaluates user subscription type, plan validity, and course purchase status before granting access to the 13 PALS simulation cases. Updated frontend redirection logic to route users to the correct simulation set (ACLS or PALS) based on the course context, and refactored the simulation access control module into a centralized, reusable pattern applicable to future courses.
impact: Enabled access to 13 PALS simulation cases across applicable user types. Established a centralized, reusable access control framework for future simulation feature additions.
learnings:
Subscription-based feature gating
Frontend-backend coordination for conditional access flows
Designing scalable feature access control systems

description: Added a timeline popup in the admin licenses dashboard that shows analysts a structured, chronological history of key status change events for any selected license — including review requests, initiation events, analyst assignments, cancellations, and expirations. Each event is timestamped and labeled with the status transition. Built a dedicated backend query to reconstruct the timeline from multiple event sources in the database, sorted and presented in a clean vertical timeline UI component. Gives analysts immediate context on the full history of a license without needing to search through other sections.
impact: Improved analyst visibility into license lifecycle events. Reduced manual cross-referencing and eliminated the need to search across multiple data sources to understand a license's history.
learnings:
Timeline-based UI for status tracking
Reconstructing event history from multiple data sources
Improving data visibility through structured chronological presentation

description: Introduced the HIPAA (Health Insurance Portability and Accountability Act) course on the platform, available at no cost to all users. Implemented a free-order flow using auto-applied discount coupons so users go through the standard checkout without being charged. Integrated full-size certificate generation via the custom Puppeteer-based certificate generator, a dedicated course quiz with hints support on failed attempts, display of the course card and plan details on the My Learning page, admin panel visibility, and full integration with the mobile app. Coordinated the WordPress side integration for course content hosting.
impact: New HIPAA course available to all users at no cost. Full end-to-end integration including ordering, quiz, hints, and full-size certificate generation.
learnings:
Course addition and integration workflow across multiple platform layers
Free course flow design with auto-applied discount logic

description: Introduced the First Aid course on the platform, available at no cost to all users. Followed the same integration pattern established for HIPAA: free-order flow via auto-applied coupons, full-size certificate generation, quiz with hints on failure, My Learning page display, admin panel visibility, and mobile app integration. The quiz covers standard first aid scenarios with a defined pass score, and upon passing users can download their full-size certificate immediately.
impact: New First Aid course available to all users at no cost. Full lifecycle integration including free ordering, quiz, and full-size certificate generation.
learnings:
Course management and addition workflow
Applying reusable course integration patterns

description: Added a refund mechanism to the user credit ledger system to handle cases where credits need to be reversed after a transaction. Implemented a role-based workflow: analysts submit a refund request with notes, which is then approved by a finance admin. Upon approval, a new zero-balance debit entry is auto-created to offset the original credit transaction, maintaining ledger immutability — no records are deleted or edited, only offset. Email notifications are sent at each stage (request submitted, approved, rejected). Finance admin access is restricted to specific authorized roles to prevent unauthorized refunds.
impact: Ensured accurate, consistent credit balances across the internal ledger and external accounting system. Every refund is auditably tracked without modifying existing transaction records.
learnings:
Designing financially consistent systems using immutable records
Role-based approval workflows for sensitive financial operations
Maintaining auditability through offset entries rather than deletions

description: Built a dedicated admin page for adding regulatory (licensing) certificates for users, replacing a cumbersome legacy flow that required navigating through multiple unrelated admin sections. The new page provides a focused form with user auto-assignment, license type selection, certificate upload, and validity date entry — reusing the existing certificate upload API without requiring new backend changes. The simplified one-page flow reduced the number of steps from several navigation hops to a single focused form, addressing analyst feedback about the legacy process being confusing and time-consuming.
impact: Reduced time and effort for analysts adding certificates. Eliminated the legacy multi-step navigation flow. Improved analyst workflow efficiency for a frequent daily task.
learnings:
Workflow simplification through focused UI design
Reusing existing APIs to avoid unnecessary backend changes
Refactoring legacy flows for usability

description: Prototyped a Stripe-based automated invoice payment flow as an alternative to QuickBooks for the licensing invoice payment system. Researched and evaluated Stripe Payment Links, Checkout Sessions, and the Stripe Invoicing product. Built a working prototype using Stripe Checkout Sessions with webhook-based payment confirmation. The prototype was ultimately abandoned in favor of consolidating all payment processing within QuickBooks, primarily because the accounts team needed invoice data, payments, and customer records in a single accounting system. Despite its superior developer experience, Stripe alone could not fully replace the accounting workflow that QuickBooks provided.
impact: Informed the final architectural decision to consolidate invoice and payment processing in QuickBooks. Produced a deep evaluation of Stripe's payment product capabilities and limitations for this use case.
learnings:
Stripe Checkout Sessions, Payment Links, and Invoicing products
Webhook integration for payment confirmation
Architectural decision-making: payment gateway vs accounting system tradeoffs

description: Developed an enhanced orders management dashboard for the admin panel, replacing a slow legacy orders list page that offered minimal filtering and no export capability. Built a new optimized API supporting advanced filtering by course, order type, plan, amount, validity period, status, and date ranges. The dashboard includes column configuration (show/hide columns), filter presets for saving frequently used filter combinations, Excel export, row-level deep links to the order detail view, and a summary row showing aggregate totals for the current filtered result set.
impact: Replaced a slow, limited legacy page with a performant, feature-rich dashboard. Enabled operational reporting via Excel export. Significantly improved order data accessibility and admin productivity.
learnings:
Designing data-heavy admin dashboards
Building advanced filtering systems with filter presets
API optimization for large order datasets

description: Introduced a feature updates section in the platform navigation — a slide-out drawer listing recently released features with category tags, release timing, brief descriptions, and direct navigation links. Content is managed by admins and is version-controlled. The feature was developed as part of SOC 2 compliance requirements to demonstrate transparency and communication of system changes to end users. Designed to be non-intrusive (drawer pattern) while keeping users informed of new capabilities without requiring a separate announcements page.
impact: Improved visibility of new features for users. Increased feature adoption through easy discoverability. Fulfilled a SOC 2 compliance transparency requirement.
learnings:
Feature announcement system development
SOC 2 compliance-driven feature design

description: Developed a dedicated licenses management dashboard for the admin panel, replacing a fragmented legacy certificates page that mixed different data types and offered limited filtering. Built a new optimized API with advanced filtering by license name, state, status, assigned analyst, date range, and validity; inline action buttons per license row (view details, assign, update status); CSV export; filter presets; and column show/hide management. The dashboard also exposes a summary section at the top showing total license counts broken down by status category for the current filtered view.
impact: Centralized license management into a single, high-performance dashboard. Eliminated navigation across multiple legacy pages. Improved data accessibility, filtering precision, and CSV reporting.
learnings:
Admin dashboard design for large license datasets
Summary metrics combined with detail table design
API performance design with complex multi-field filtering

description: Built a custom automated PDF generation system for full-size course completion certificates using Puppeteer, replacing a slow manual process that required support team intervention for every request. The system renders an HTML certificate template (with user name, course name, completion date, certificate ID, and course-specific branding) in a headless browser and exports it as a high-quality PDF, which is then stored and linked to the course order. Researched and benchmarked multiple PDF generation libraries (pdfkit, pdflib, html-pdf, puppeteer) before selecting Puppeteer for its layout accuracy, HTML/CSS support, and generation speed. Certificate templates are designed per supported course to ensure accurate branding and layout.
impact: Certificate generation reduced from hours (manual process) to seconds (automated API). Eliminated dependency on support team for certificate creation. Consistent, branded PDF output across all supported courses.
learnings:
Custom PDF generation with Puppeteer and headless browser rendering
PDF library benchmarking and selection
Course certificate template design

description: Developed a unified certificates management dashboard consolidating three distinct certificate types — Provider Cards, CME Certificates, and Full-Size Certificates — into a single admin interface with a tab-based switcher. Each certificate type has its own dedicated optimized API and filter set (course, date range, user email, status). Shared features across all tabs include CSV export, column management, pagination, and quick-view links to the actual generated certificate files. Previously, admins had to navigate across different legacy pages to manage each certificate type.
impact: Centralized certificate management for all certificate types in a single view. Eliminated navigation across fragmented legacy pages. Improved data accessibility and reporting.
learnings:
Multi-type data dashboard design
Per-entity API design for certificate data
Admin panel efficiency improvement through consolidation

task: Certificate Task Acknowledgement Approval by Admin
description: Added an admin-level approval layer on top of the analyst weekly certificate task acknowledgement system. Admins can view the latest acknowledgement submitted by each analyst for any certificate task and either approve or reject it with mandatory notes. A history popup shows the full chronological log of all past acknowledgements for a task, each with its approval decision, admin notes, and timestamps. Role-based access ensures only authorized admins can perform approvals. Rejection triggers a notification back to the analyst indicating the need to re-acknowledge.
impact: Added structured admin oversight to the analyst task acknowledgement workflow. Provides a full, auditable history of approval decisions per task.
learnings:
Approval and rejection workflow design with audit trails
Role-gated admin action patterns

description: Led the full frontend implementation of a major header redesign across the connect platform based on approved Figma designs. The new header introduced a restructured two-level navigation with updated branding, primary service navigation, user profile controls, and notification indicators. Converted the React component implementation to semantic HTML for cross-platform reuse, provided the resulting HTML file to the Wordpress team so all platforms could maintain a visually identical header. Applied precise responsive breakpoints for desktop, tablet, and mobile views. Coordinated multiple rounds of review to achieve pixel-accurate alignment with the Figma spec.
impact: Visually consistent header across all web platforms. Single-source HTML reference enables future header changes to propagate across platforms. Established mobile-responsive header behavior.
learnings:
Pixel-accurate component implementation from design specs
Multi-platform UI consistency through shared HTML reference
React component to portable HTML conversion

description: Designed and built a complete ledger-based credit management system modeled on a banking passbook architecture, ensuring every credit transaction is immutably recorded. The system supports credit additions (admin-initiated, product-specific), deductions (invoice payment, manual), and refunds — each stored as separate immutable rows with a running balance calculated from the full transaction history. Every entry is attributed to the analyst who performed the action and linked to the relevant product or invoice. Integrated across the admin panel (add/deduct credits, transaction history dashboard), the invoices system (automatic deduction on invoice creation when user has credits), and the connect platform (live balance display for users). No record is ever edited or deleted; all corrections use offsetting entries.
impact: Centralized, auditable credit management with complete transaction history. Immutable records ensure financial accuracy and prevent discrepancies. Real-time balance visible to users on the platform.
learnings:
Ledger-based system architecture for financial transaction tracking
Immutable record design with offset entries for corrections
Maintaining running balance accuracy across concurrent operations

task: Bug Fix: Open Route Session Expiry Logout
description: Fixed a significant UX bug where users visiting public (open route) pages — such as the Help Center, which is accessible without login — were being incorrectly redirected to the login page when their background session expired, even though those pages do not require authentication. Root cause: a global Axios 401 interceptor was unconditionally redirecting on any session expiry regardless of the current route type. Fix: implemented route-aware logic in the interceptor that checks whether the current page is a protected or public route before redirecting — on public routes, the page is refreshed in place rather than redirecting to login.
impact: Fixed disruptive incorrect login redirections on public pages. Ensured proper separation of protected vs public route session behavior. Improved user experience for unauthenticated browsing.
learnings:
Session management and Axios interceptor design
Route-aware authentication logic
Handling 401 responses gracefully across mixed-access applications

description: Built a full-stack conference registration website for healthcare professional events from scratch. The site consists of multiple pages: Home (event details and speaker info), Abstract Submission (form for submitting research abstracts), Review Panel (reviewer access to submitted abstracts), Registration (delegate registration form with plan selection), and Payment. Supported multiple registration plan tiers in both INR and USD. Implemented Razorpay for domestic (INR) payments and Stripe for international (USD) payments, both with webhook-based payment confirmation. Automated email notifications for registration confirmation, payment receipt, and event invitation. Built with Vite and React as a standalone project.
impact: End-to-end conference registration platform supporting multi-currency payments. Automated the registration and notification workflow. Provided abstract submission and review infrastructure.
learnings:
Full-stack website development with Vite and React
Razorpay and Stripe dual-currency payment gateway integration
Webhook-based payment confirmation and status sync

description: Implemented a secure email-based OTP (One-Time Password) verification step in the user registration flow, requiring new users to verify ownership of their email address before completing account creation. The OTP is a 6-digit numeric code encrypted and embedded in a short-lived JWT token, sent to the user's email. On submission, the backend decrypts the JWT, validates the OTP, checks expiry, and completes registration only on success. The OTP UI was designed independently without UI/UX team involvement. Handles resend with rate limiting, expired OTP gracefully, and incorrect OTP with attempt tracking.
impact: Prevented spam and fake account registrations. Ensured only users with valid email access can create accounts. Secured plan-specific benefits to verified users.
learnings:
OTP generation, encryption, and JWT-based token validation
Multi-step authentication flow design
Rate limiting and attempt management for verification systems

description: Integrated the `serve` npm package to enable local preview of production builds before deployment. Added a `npm run preview` command that first runs the production build and then serves the dist output locally on a configurable port, replicating the production serving behavior. This allowed catching build-specific issues (such as asset path resolution differences between dev and prod, route fallback behavior, and environment variable substitution) before they reached the production environment.
impact: Enabled pre-deployment production build validation. Allowed catching environment-specific issues locally before release. Improved developer confidence in each deployment.
learnings:
Production build validation strategies
Differences between development server and production serving behavior

description: Introduced automated code formatting across the entire frontend codebase using Prettier. Defined a consistent formatting configuration (print width, trailing commas, semicolons, quote style) and committed it to the repository. Added a format npm script and applied formatting to over 350 files in a single batch operation, verified that no functional changes were introduced, and updated the development guide to include formatting as a pre-commit step. This was the first time formal formatting standards were established for the codebase.
impact: Standardized code style across 350+ files. Improved readability and reduced noise in code reviews from inconsistent formatting. Established a shared formatting standard for the team.
learnings:
Codebase standardization with automated tooling
Managing large-scale formatting changes safely
Improving team developer experience through consistency

description: Developed an admin-authenticated API that accepts a list of database table names in the request payload and selectively syncs (alters) only those tables, returning a per-table success/error summary in the response. This eliminated the need for direct server access every time a schema change needed to be applied — previously, schema syncing required either a full-database sync (risky) or direct server administrator involvement. The API is protected behind admin-only authentication and returns detailed results indicating which tables were synced, which were skipped, and any errors encountered.
impact: Eliminated server dependency for schema updates. Enabled controlled, targeted table syncing via API. Reduced risk of accidental full-database schema alterations.
learnings:
Admin-level internal tooling API design
Safe, targeted database schema update patterns
Designing operations with granular result reporting

description: Built a command-line utility script to selectively sync individual database tables by name using Sequelize's `alter: true` sync mode, as an alternative to the full `.sync({ alter: true })` call which alters every table in the database. The script accepts table names as CLI arguments, dynamically loads only the specified Sequelize models, and runs alter sync on those tables only. This was the predecessor to the Table Sync API and is used directly on the server during development or urgent patch situations.
impact: Eliminated the risk of accidentally altering unrelated tables during development. Reduced database sync operation scope from global to targeted.
learnings:
Sequelize model-level selective sync
Building CLI utilities with argument parsing in Node.js
Safe database schema update practices during development

description: Built a custom PDF provider card generator using Puppeteer to replace a dependency on a slow, frequently failing Wordpress-based API. The generator renders an HTML card template in a headless Chromium browser, injecting user details (name, designation, course, completion date) and applying course-specific color themes and branding. The resulting PDF is stored server-side and a download link returned to the client. Benchmarked multiple PDF libraries (pdfkit, pdflib, html-pdf, puppeteer) before selecting Puppeteer for its pixel-accurate HTML rendering, CSS support, and consistent output. Addressed a date-mismatch bug by setting the server-side timezone explicitly during rendering to prevent UTC vs IST discrepancies on certificate dates. Integrated across the connect platform, mobile app, and admin panel.
impact: Provider card generation time reduced from over 3 seconds to 500ms–1s. Eliminated Wordpress API dependency. Consistent, accurate PDF layout across all supported courses.
learnings:
Puppeteer-based PDF generation with headless browser rendering
Server-side timezone handling for accurate date rendering
PDF library evaluation and selection
Eliminating third-party API dependencies

description: Enabled CME (Continuing Medical Education) certificate generation for the NRP (Neonatal Resuscitation Program) course, allowing users who complete the NRP quiz to claim CME credits and download their CME certificate. The integration involved: backend API updates to support NRP as a CME-eligible course, creation of a dedicated NRP survey form (used for CME credit validation by the CME accrediting body), frontend display of the CME certificate download option on the course completion page, CME credit count display in the applicable subscription plan UI, and full integration with the mobile app. Coordinated with the WordPress team for the CME certificate generation backend.
impact: New CME certificate benefit available for NRP course users across web and mobile platforms.
learnings:
CME certificate integration workflow for new course types
Cross-platform feature integration (web + mobile app)

description: Built a self-service invoices page for licensing users on the connect platform, giving providers visibility into their licensing invoice history without requiring them to contact the support team. The page shows a filterable table of invoice line items with filters for date range, license type, and invoice status (pending, paid, overdue); sort options; and a detail view per invoice showing the breakdown of line items, amounts, and payment status. Previously, users had no direct visibility into their licensing invoice data from the platform.
impact: New self-service invoice visibility for licensing users. Reduced reliance on support team for invoice status inquiries.
learnings:
Client-facing financial data dashboard design
User-centric invoice presentation

description: Added a dedicated invoice items section to the admin panel, providing the accounts and operations teams with a centralized view of individual invoice line items across all licensing invoices. The dashboard supports filtering by date range, license type, invoice status, provider email, and amount; sort options; and CSV export for accounting reconciliation. Invoice items represent the granular fee breakdown (service fees, application fees, verification fees, card processing fees) that make up each invoice, which were previously only visible inside individual invoice detail pages.
impact: Centralized invoice line item management for admin and accounts teams. Enabled CSV export for accounting reconciliation and reporting.
learnings:
Financial data granularity in admin dashboards
Separating invoice-level vs line-item-level views

description: Developed an internal quiz automation tool for development and QA use. When activated (after password verification to prevent misuse), the tool automatically selects answers for all quiz questions — either all correct or all incorrect depending on the mode selected — and advances through the quiz to completion. This enabled QA to validate the full course completion flow (quiz → certificates → order benefits) without manually answering every question for each test scenario.
impact: Significantly reduced manual QA testing effort. Enabled faster validation of course completion flows across all courses and user types.
learnings:
Internal developer productivity tool design
Password-protected tool access patterns
QA workflow efficiency through automation

task: Prebuild Validation Script for Production Safety
description: Developed a custom Node.js prebuild validation script that automatically scans the entire codebase before every production build, checking for: hardcoded staging or localhost URLs, environment-specific constants or feature flags that should not reach production, and any restricted patterns that were previously identified as production issues. The script runs automatically as a pre-build hook and can also be triggered manually via a dedicated npm command. If any violations are found, the build is blocked and the offending files/lines are listed. The script is configurable with allowlist patterns for false-positive suppression.
impact: Eliminated the risk of environment-specific code leaking into production builds. Blocked multiple near-misses during post-implementation. Established a mandatory safety gate in the deployment workflow.
learnings:
Pre-build script development integrated with npm lifecycle hooks
Pattern-based codebase scanning
Build security and release reliability

description: Introduced the ECG (Electrocardiogram interpretation) course on the platform, available free to all users without requiring a course order or payment. The course features a quiz, free access flow (bypassing the order requirement), and quiz analytics dashboard integration. Documented a comprehensive full-stack course integration guide covering all required frontend changes (My Learning page, course card, navigation), backend changes (access control, order logic, analytics), and mobile app integration — establishing a reusable reference for all future course onboarding tasks.
impact: New free course available to all users with no order required. Integration guide reduced future course onboarding effort for the team.
learnings:
Course management and no-order-required access flow design
Documenting integration patterns for scalable course onboarding

description: Built a public Help Center page accessible to both unauthenticated visitors and logged-in users, featuring a searchable FAQ system organized by categories (account management, courses, licensing, billing, etc.). Each FAQ entry tracks view counts to surface the most frequently accessed questions. The page also includes a support inquiry form that sends the user's message and contact details via email to the support team. The open-route access required separate session handling to avoid triggering login redirects when users are not authenticated.
impact: New self-service FAQ resource accessible to all users. Provides a direct support inquiry pathway. View tracking enables data-driven prioritization of FAQ content.
learnings:
Open route page design with session-aware behavior
FAQ system with search, categories, and view tracking

description: Built an admin dashboard for managing Help Center FAQ content end-to-end. Features include: add/edit FAQ forms with a rich text editor for formatted answers, category management, change log tracking that records who made what change and when (full audit trail), view count analytics per question showing which FAQs are most accessed, and category-based filtering to navigate large FAQ sets. Built alongside the public Help Center page to provide a complete content management solution without requiring external CMS tools.
impact: Complete content management for Help Center FAQs without external CMS. Full audit trail of content changes. View analytics to guide content prioritization.
learnings:
CMS-style dashboard development
Audit trail implementation for content changes
Rich text editor integration in admin forms

description: Migrated the React frontend from the deprecated create-react-app (CRA) toolchain to Vite with Node 22. The migration involved reconfiguring the build pipeline, converting CRA-specific environment variable patterns to Vite's import.meta.env format, resolving module resolution differences, updating the proxy configuration for development API calls, and adjusting path aliases. Following migration, the production build size dropped by ~42%, development server startup time improved by ~93%, and hot module replacement became near-instantaneous.
impact: Production build size reduced by ~42%. Development server startup time reduced by ~93%. Hot module replacement became near-instantaneous.
learnings:
Vite build tool configuration and plugin setup
Migrating from CRA to Vite: env variable patterns, module resolution, dev proxy
Build optimization with modern bundlers

description: Completely redesigned the My Learning API query architecture to achieve O(1) query complexity regardless of the number of courses a user is enrolled in. The prior implementation executed 4 separate SQL queries per course in a sequential loop, meaning a user enrolled in 10 courses triggered 40 sequential queries. The redesign replaced this with 4 parallel queries that fetch data for all enrolled courses in bulk using `IN` clauses, then map the results to each course in memory using JavaScript `Map` lookups. Executed the 4 bulk queries concurrently using `Promise.all` to maximize throughput. Response time dropped by ~70% for typical users.
impact: API response time reduced from 1.5–2.5s to ~400ms. SQL query count reduced from O(N×4) to a constant 4 parallel queries regardless of enrollment size.
learnings:
API performance engineering and query complexity analysis
O(N) to O(1) query redesign using bulk fetching and in-memory mapping
Parallel query execution with Promise.all

description: Implemented a draft schedule feature in the scheduling section, allowing scheduling users to create and save draft shifts before committing them as confirmed scheduled shifts. Draft shifts are visually distinct on the calendar (different color/style) and can be edited, confirmed, or discarded. Built using the FullCalendar library's drag-and-drop and event rendering APIs to enable intuitive shift placement. The draft-to-confirmed promotion flow triggers the standard shift confirmation logic and notifications.
impact: Enabled a draft-first scheduling workflow, reducing accidental confirmed shift creation. Users can plan shifts before committing.
learnings:
FullCalendar library event rendering and drag-and-drop APIs
Draft vs confirmed state management in scheduling UIs

description: Redesigned the post-quiz course completion flow to improve clarity and capture additional user engagement data. Changes: mandatory course feedback form on first quiz pass (skippable on revisit), a new post-quiz result screen with dedicated provider card download and CME certificate download sections, persistent display of the user's quiz score when returning to the course page (previously the score was lost after the first visit), and enforcement of mandatory simulation completion before quiz access for certain premium plans. Coordinated with multiple team members on frontend and backend changes simultaneously.
impact: Improved course completion UX with clearer certificate access. Mandatory feedback collection introduced. Persistent quiz score display on course revisit. Simulation gate enforced for applicable plan types.
learnings:
Course completion flow architecture
Coordinating multi-team feature delivery
User experience design for multi-step learning workflows

description: Audited all npm dependencies in the frontend project and identified 53 packages across 7 categories that were no longer used: legacy Material-UI v4 packages (replaced by MUI v5), deprecated content rendering libraries, unused form input libraries, duplicate utility packages, and abandoned authentication helpers. Systematically removed each package, verified the build still succeeded after each batch removal, and confirmed no runtime regressions with QA. Build size reduced noticeably and npm install time decreased.
impact: Removed 53 unused packages. Build size and npm install time reduced. Reduced security surface area.
learnings:
Dependency audit methodology
Safe systematic package removal with incremental verification
Build size impact analysis

description: Added proactive email alert notifications to developers when provider card or CME certificate generation fails. The notification email includes: the user's email and ID, the course name, the quiz attempt ID for tracing the exact attempt in the database, the error type (e.g., Puppeteer crash, storage write failure, API timeout), and the full error stack trace. Previously, certificate generation failures were silent — users would encounter a broken experience without any developer awareness until a support ticket was filed. The alerts enabled same-day detection and resolution in most cases.
impact: Enabled proactive, real-time detection of certificate generation failures. Reduced average time-to-fix for certificate issues from days to hours.
learnings:
Internal failure alerting system design
Structured error notifications with diagnostic context

description: Resolved critical build generation failures caused by a breaking incompatibility between the latest `@mui/x-date-pickers` version and the project's Node 16 / React 18 environment. The latest version introduced peer dependency requirements that conflicted with existing packages. Investigated the compatibility matrix, downgraded to the last compatible stable version, verified that all date validation logic, formatting, and locale handling remained intact across all affected components, and confirmed the build generation succeeded without errors.
impact: Resolved build generation failures blocking deployments. Restored full date picker functionality across all affected admin panel components.
learnings:
npm package compatibility matrix analysis
Downgrade strategies that preserve functionality
Diagnosing peer dependency conflicts in React/MUI projects

description: Improved My Learning API response time by 60% by identifying and eliminating a dependency on an unreliable external LMS API that was being called on every request to fetch course progress percentages. The LMS API had high latency (~1.5s average) and frequent timeout failures. Replaced it with direct queries to the internal user progress table, which already stored the same progress data with sub-100ms query times. Validated data consistency between the two sources before cutting over, and removed the LMS API call and its associated timeout/fallback error handling.
impact: Response time reduced from 2.5–3s to ~1s. Eliminated dependency on an unreliable external LMS API. Improved reliability (no more LMS timeout failures).
learnings:
API optimization by eliminating external call dependencies
Data consistency validation before source cutover
Building reliable internal data sources to replace external ones

description: Added a quiz attempt ID column to the orders table, creating a direct link between a user's completed quiz attempt and their course order. When a user passes the course quiz, the quiz attempt unique ID is stored against the order. This serves two purposes: (1) enables persistent quiz score retrieval on the course page by looking up the linked attempt from the orders table rather than re-querying the quiz logs, and (2) supports the one-attempt enforcement logic for course benefits — once an attempt is linked to an order and benefits are claimed, the system can verify no re-generation is possible.
impact: Enables persistent quiz score display against course orders. Provides the foundation for benefit enforcement and one-attempt generation logic.
learnings:
Data linking patterns across related tables
Foundational schema changes that enable downstream features

description: Performed a large-scale cleanup by removing deprecated V1 and V2 route sets along with 301 associated obsolete files and folders (old page components, legacy utilities, unused assets, and abandoned feature modules). Carefully mapped all references to the deprecated routes to confirm none were still active in the current codebase before deletion. The build size dropped significantly as the removed code had been bundled into the production output despite being unreachable. This was a precursor to the Vite migration, reducing the total scope of the migration.
impact: Build size reduced by 58% after removal of 301 legacy files. Improved codebase clarity and reduced future maintenance burden.
learnings:
Safe legacy code removal through reference mapping
Build size impact of bundled dead code
Codebase archaeology to identify safely removable code

task: Quiz Hints Feature After Failed Attempt
description: Added a hints section to the failed quiz result screen, showing users targeted feedback on only the questions they got wrong. For each incorrect question, the user sees the question text, their selected answer, and a subtle indicator to help guide their next attempt without outright revealing the correct answer. Special handling is included for multi-select questions — a question is marked as incorrect even if the user selected some (but not all) correct options, and the hint indicates the partial selection. The hints section is shown only on the fail screen and is absent from the pass screen.
impact: Improved learning experience by providing targeted post-failure guidance. Helps users understand their mistakes before retrying, increasing retry pass rates.
learnings:
Quiz result analysis and conditional UI rendering
Handling multi-select question partial-correctness logic

description: Added a user-facing error screen for the scenario where provider card generation fails, replacing a previously broken experience (blank screen or silent failure). The error screen shows a user-friendly explanation, displays the specific API error message in a collapsible technical details section for support team use, and provides a 'Contact Support' button that pre-fills a support email with the user's details and the error context. Previously, failed generation left users with no feedback, leading to confused support tickets.
impact: Users receive clear guidance and a support pathway when certificate generation fails. Support team receives structured pre-filled reports, improving resolution speed.
learnings:
Error state UX design
Contextual support escalation patterns in error screens

description: Performed a major navigation and codebase restructuring across the connect platform spanning 750 file changes. Introduced three new primary navigation sections (Monitoring & Renewal, Acquisition, Tools & Resources) to better organize the growing feature set. Upgraded all pages within the restructured sections from MUI v4 to MUI v5, removed unused legacy authentication pages, cleaned up stale image assets, and eliminated redundant API calls that were being fired on page loads that no longer required them. The restructuring reduced the production build size significantly.
impact: Improved navigation clarity and user journey. Build size reduced significantly. MUI v4 → v5 migration for restructured pages. Eliminated redundant API calls.
learnings:
Large-scale project restructuring with 750+ file changes
MUI v4 to v5 migration patterns
Build size reduction through asset and dependency cleanup

description: Designed and built the foundational My Learning API — a unified endpoint that consolidates all course-related data for a user into a single response, serving as the single source of truth for course status across the web platform, mobile app, and WordPress site. The API computes and returns: enrolled courses list, order validity, course progress percentage, provider card generation status (generated / not generated / certificate ID), CME certificate status, full-size certificate status, and the current actionable button state for each course (e.g., Start, Resume, View Certificate). This eliminated the need for each platform to make multiple separate API calls and perform their own state calculation logic. Integrated with documentation for the mobile app and WordPress teams.
impact: Unified course data source across all three platforms. Eliminated multiple redundant API calls per page load. Standardized course state calculation. Reduced frontend data processing complexity.
learnings:
Cross-platform API design as a single source of truth
Aggregating heterogeneous data sources into a unified response
API documentation for multi-team consumption

description: Enabled CME certificate generation for the NIHSS (National Institutes of Health Stroke Scale) course, allowing users who complete the NIHSS quiz to claim CME credits. Changes included backend API updates to mark NIHSS as CME-eligible, a dedicated CME survey form for the course, frontend integration on the course completion page, and mobile app integration. The NIHSS course was already live with free access; this enhancement added the CME certificate as an additional benefit for completing the course.
impact: Added CME certificate benefit to the existing NIHSS course across web and mobile platforms.
learnings:
Adding CME benefits to existing live courses without disrupting access
Cross-platform CME integration

description: Implemented a password vault feature for licensing users on the connect platform, allowing them to securely store and retrieve credentials for external licensing portals (state medical board sites, credentialing databases, etc.) associated with specific licensing jobs. Each vault entry stores site name, URL, username, password, and 2FA status. Entries are scoped per licensing job so analysts can quickly look up credentials during active licensing work without leaving the platform.
impact: New in-platform credential management tool for licensing professionals. Reduced context-switching and credential lookup time during licensing work.
learnings:
Password vault UI/UX design
Job-scoped credential storage patterns

description: Enabled CME certificate generation for the ASC CE (Ambulatory Surgical Center Continuing Education) course, including CME survey form integration, backend API updates, and frontend changes to display the CME credit count and benefit details in the course plan purchase popup. Also updated the total CME credit count for full access plan holders to include ASC CE credits. CME certificate generation was integrated with the mobile app alongside the web platform. Coordinated with the WordPress developer for the backend CME certificate generation component.
impact: Added CME certificate benefit for ASC CE course users. Updated plan-level CME credit counts to reflect the new course. Cross-platform integration on web and mobile.
learnings:
CME benefit integration for a new course type
Coordinating cross-team (WordPress + mobile) integration

task: Connect Admin View for Hospital Admins
description: Developed the frontend implementation of a hospital admin view on the connect platform, providing hospital administrators with visibility into their provider roster data. The view consists of three sections: Dashboard (overview charts using react-apexcharts showing provider counts by status with bar and donut chart visualizations), Acquisition (providers in the licensing acquisition process), and Monitoring & Renewal (license expiry tracking and renewal status). APIs were provided by backend team members; the work focused on complete frontend implementation including chart configuration, table design, route-based access control, and role-gated navigation to ensure only hospital admins can access the view.
impact: Provided hospital administrators with direct visibility into their provider data and licensing pipeline. Advanced data management view with chart and table presentation.
learnings:
react-apexcharts bar and donut chart configuration
Role-based route access control implementation
Frontend-only delivery with API-provided backend

task: Quiz Enhancement: Back Button & UI Improvements
description: Enhanced the quiz interface with three improvements: (1) a Back button allowing users to navigate to any previously answered question, (2) a redesigned option button layout with updated visual styling, and (3) a progress tracker component showing the current question number out of total. The back button required a backend change: the quiz log API was refactored to perform an upsert — updating an existing log entry if the user changes their selected answer for a previously answered question, rather than inserting a duplicate entry. This ensures accurate final-state tracking in the quiz logs for analytics and scoring.
impact: Users can review and change answers before final quiz submission. Improved quiz UX and answer accuracy. Quiz log entries now correctly reflect the user's final selection per question.
learnings:
Quiz state and navigation management
Upsert patterns for tracking mutable user selections
Full-stack quiz UI enhancement

description: Integrated the NIHSS (National Institutes of Health Stroke Scale) course onto the connect platform with free access for all users — no order or payment required. The NIHSS course assesses a user's ability to evaluate stroke severity using a standardized 15-item scale quiz. Configured the quiz with 14 questions and a passing criterion of at least 11 correct answers. Integrated the course into the quiz analytics dashboard for attempt tracking. The course was also made available on the mobile app.
impact: New free NIHSS course available to all platform users. Quiz analytics tracking integrated from launch.
learnings:
New course integration pattern
Free-access course flow without order requirements

description: Automated the provider card generation process upon quiz passing, eliminating a 4-step manual process that many users were abandoning midway through. Previously, users had to: click 'Get Provider Card', confirm their name in a popup, review a course benefits screen, then click 'Done' to trigger generation — steps that frequently resulted in incomplete actions and support tickets. The new system monitors quiz completion status, and on a passing attempt, automatically calls the certificate generation API, stores the returned certificate ID against the course order (using the order benefits system), and marks the benefit as claimed, preventing re-generation. The user sees their provider card available immediately on the course page after passing.
impact: Eliminated provider card generation issues for users. Significantly reduced related support ticket volume. Automated course completion benefit tracking.
learnings:
Workflow automation by eliminating user-initiated steps
Support ticket root cause analysis and resolution
Event-driven benefit claiming on quiz completion

description: Added a JSON-typed benefits column to the orders table to store certificate IDs (provider card, CME certificate, full-size certificate) against each course order. Built an API that accepts an order ID, a benefit key (provider_card / cme_certificate / full_size_certificate), and a benefit value (certificate ID), and stores or updates the corresponding benefit entry for that order. This enables the system to check whether a specific benefit has already been generated for an order (preventing duplicates) and to retrieve stored certificate IDs for persistent display on the course page. Integrated across the web platform and mobile app.
impact: Enabled tracking of which benefits (certificates) have been generated per course order. Prevents duplicate certificate generation. Cross-platform benefit state consistency.
learnings:
JSON column usage for flexible benefit key-value storage
Cross-platform API design
Benefit state tracking patterns in order management

description: Built a comprehensive quiz attempt analytics dashboard for the admin panel providing two views: a table view and a chart view. The table view shows a per-course summary (user count, total attempts, passed, failed) and a detailed individual attempt breakdown (user email, date, duration in hh:mm:ss, correct/total questions, score percentage, pass/fail status). The chart view shows a daily quiz attempts line chart using react-apexcharts with time frame filters (1D, 1W, 1M, 1Y, ALL) and platform filters (web/app). Advanced features include filter presets, column management, data export, exclusion filters for internal test accounts, and a dashboard information popup explaining each metric. Dashboard data refreshes automatically on filter change.
impact: Real-time quiz attempt analytics across all courses and platforms. Enables data-driven course improvement and QA decisions. Provides visibility into attempt trends over time.
learnings:
Analytics dashboard development with multi-view design
react-apexcharts line chart with dynamic time frames
Query optimization for large quiz log datasets

description: Designed and implemented a real-time quiz activity tracking system that logs every question and selected answer during a quiz attempt, providing a persistent, granular record of each user's quiz session. A unique attempt ID (formatted as userID_timestamp) is generated when the user starts a quiz, and every option selection fires a log API call with the question ID, selected option number, correctness flag, and platform (web/app). If the user changes their answer and resubmits, the existing log entry is updated rather than duplicated. The tracking system was integrated into both the connect web platform and the mobile app. As the most heavily used feature across the platform, the log table grew to over 1.2 million rows within its first year — providing a rich dataset for quiz analytics, support query verification, and pass score auditing.
impact: Complete per-question quiz tracking across web and mobile. Enables support query verification of quiz completion claims. Powers the quiz analytics dashboard. Grew to 1.2M+ rows as the most active table.
learnings:
High-volume activity tracking system design
Working with large, rapidly growing database tables
Cross-platform API consistency for tracking events

description: Built a full-stack journal manuscript management system for the admin panel, enabling the content and journal teams to manage manuscripts through a multi-stage publication workflow. Features include: a manuscript list with filtering by stage, assigned team, and submission date; a stage progression interface (initial copyediting → QA → QI → layout → publication); per-manuscript detail views showing all submitted files, reviewer notes, and revision history; change log tracking with a full audit trail of who moved a manuscript to which stage and when; and assignment management to route manuscripts between team members. Database schema was designed to support the multi-stage progression with proper relational integrity between manuscripts, stages, assignments, and audit records.
impact: Centralized journal manuscript management system for the content and journal teams. Full audit trail of all stage changes. Replaced a disjointed email-based manuscript tracking process.
learnings:
Multi-stage workflow system design
Audit trail and change log implementation
Relational database schema design for workflow state management

description: Built the main home dashboard page for the connect platform — the first page users see after signing in. The dashboard presents a consolidated view of the user's activity across all platform services: state licensing section (task counts for completed, timely, and overdue licenses visualized as a donut chart using react-apexcharts, plus acquisition tasks in progress), course progress section (list of enrolled courses with progress bars and current status), and certificates section (counts of generated provider cards, CME certificates, and full-size certificates). Designed to give users immediate situational awareness of their licensing and learning status without requiring navigation to individual sections.
impact: Centralized dashboard giving users an at-a-glance view of their licensing, course, and certificate status immediately on sign-in. Reduced navigation required to check status across services.
learnings:
User-facing dashboard design for multi-service platforms
react-apexcharts donut chart for status distribution visualization

task: Certificate Task Acknowledgement — Analyst Weekly Tracking
description: Built a weekly certificate task acknowledgement system requiring analysts to acknowledge each of their assigned certificate tasks at the start of every week (Mondays). The acknowledgement confirms the analyst is aware of and actively working on each task. An action button in the certificate task dashboard allows one acknowledgement per task per week. Acknowledgements are reset automatically every Sunday at midnight via a CRON job, which also sends email reminders to analysts who have not yet acknowledged their tasks for the new week. The button is disabled after acknowledgement and re-enabled after the weekly reset. A separate admin approval workflow was subsequently built on top of this system to add management oversight.
impact: Established weekly accountability for certificate task management across the analyst team. Enabled management visibility into acknowledgement compliance.
learnings:
CRON job scheduling for weekly resets
Email notification workflows triggered by CRON execution
Database design for time-bounded acknowledgement tracking

description: Developed a dedicated benefits program portal page on the connect platform for enrolled users, displaying their active program benefits and eligibility details. The program benefits shown include discounted professional services, free access to certificate courses, waived journal publication fees, ongoing CME compliance monitoring, and additional professional services. A backend flag on user accounts indicates program enrollment, and the portal page is conditionally visible based on enrollment status. Additionally built a multi-user registration API allowing a hospital or organization to register multiple users simultaneously and assign them to the benefits program in a single API call — used for onboarding hospital groups onto the program.
impact: New dedicated portal for benefits program users showing their active entitlements. Bulk registration API enabled efficient hospital-level onboarding.
learnings:
Conditional page visibility based on user enrollment flags
Bulk user creation with hospital assignment

description: Built a white-theme Career section for the connect platform, serving US-based users with three sub-sections: Job Board, Locums, and Contact. The Job Board allows users to browse available positions with multi-select filter panels (job type, profession, state, status, specialty), a keyword search field, and tabs for saved jobs and applied jobs — users can save jobs for later and track their application history. The Locums section showcases locum tenens staffing opportunities with contact details. The Contact section provides staffing inquiry forms. The entire section uses a clean white theme consistent with the platform redesign.
impact: Provided a dedicated career and job discovery section for healthcare professionals. Enhanced job browsing with multi-filter search, saved jobs, and application tracking.
learnings:
Job portal UI/UX with advanced filtering and sorting
Saved items and application history management
Multi-section content page design

description: Led the end-to-end redesign of the connect platform from a legacy dark-themed UI to a modern white theme aligned with the company's other platforms. Developed a common page layout shared across all platform sections, consisting of a primary header (with navigation, user profile, and notifications) and a secondary navigation header. The redesigned home page features a course plan carousel showcasing ACLS, BLS, and PALS plans, and a services navigation tab panel providing access to State Licenses, Certificates, CME Compliance, Schedule, and Career sections — each with sub-navigation for deeper service areas. All existing page components were migrated to the new layout while preserving full functionality.
impact: Modern, visually consistent platform design aligned with company-wide design standards. Improved usability through cleaner layout, clearer navigation hierarchy, and updated typography.
learnings:
Large-scale platform redesign while preserving existing functionality
Shared layout component design for consistent page structure
MUI component customization for white theme implementation

description: Built the My Learning page as a central course hub for users, introduced as part of the platform redesign. The page displays all available platform courses as cards showing course name, current status (not purchased, in progress, completed), and a quick-action button that adapts based on the user's course state (Explore Plans, Start Course, Resume, View Certificate). An 'Explore Plans' popup allows users to view and purchase available course plans directly from the learning dashboard without navigating to a separate purchase page. A Full Access Plan promotional banner is shown to users who haven't purchased the bundle. Designed to visually mirror the course experience on the Wordpress marketing site for a consistent user journey.
impact: Unified course discovery, purchase, and access from a single dashboard. Replaced a fragmented multi-page course navigation experience. Contextual action buttons reduce steps to course access.
learnings:
Dynamic button state management based on course enrollment and completion
In-page plan purchase flow design
React Context for shared course data management across the page

description: Built a shift payment request feature for scheduling users (hospital-based healthcare workers), allowing them to submit payment claims for completed shifts within a configurable date range (up to one month prior to today). Developed three interfaces: a payment request submission page where users select a date range and confirm shift hours, a payment history page showing all submitted requests with status tracking (pending, approved, rejected), and an admin-side payment management dashboard where administrators can review, filter, approve, or reject payment requests with notes. The feature integrates with the existing scheduling and shift data to pre-populate shift hours in the request form.
impact: New self-service payment claim workflow for scheduling users. Full payment request lifecycle from submission to approval. Admin payment management dashboard with filtering and bulk actions.
learnings:
Multi-role feature development (user-facing + admin)
Paginated dashboard development with MUI table and pagination components
Shift data integration for payment pre-population

description: Resolved persistent session expiry and redirection issues by implementing an in-page re-login popup that appears when a user's session token expires during an active session. Per SOC 2 compliance requirements, session tokens have a short expiry, which was causing users to be unexpectedly redirected to the login page mid-task — losing any in-progress work. The session end popup overlays the current page and allows the user to re-enter their credentials and re-authenticate without losing their current location or context. Implemented on both the admin panel and the connect platform. The popup is triggered by token expiry detection in the Axios interceptor and shows a countdown to auto-logout if not acted upon.
impact: Eliminated disruptive mid-session redirects to login. Users can re-authenticate in place without losing current page context. Resolved a recurring reported issue from the licensing and admin teams.
learnings:
JWT token expiry detection and inline re-authentication flows
Session management in SOC 2 compliant applications
In-page modal re-login UX design

task: Auth Token Refresh During Course Navigation
description: Implemented an automatic token refresh mechanism to prevent users from being logged out during active course navigation due to session token expiry. The short token expiry required by SOC 2 compliance was causing users to be logged out mid-course, generating support tickets. The solution introduces a context-aware token extension: when a user navigates to any course unit page, the system issues an extended session token; when the user enters a deep course interaction (quiz, simulation), the token expiry is extended further. Token refresh is handled transparently in the background via an API call on route change within the course navigation, without interrupting the user experience.
impact: Eliminated session timeout interruptions during course navigation. Resolved a class of support queries from users being logged out mid-course or mid-quiz.
learnings:
Context-aware JWT token refresh mechanism design
Balancing SOC 2 token expiry requirements with UX continuity
Background token refresh without user interruption

description: Resolved all security vulnerabilities identified in the company's 2024 VAPT (Vulnerability Assessment and Penetration Testing) audit report, conducted by an external security assessment firm, to maintain SOC Type 2 certification. The audit identified multiple vulnerabilities across both the connect platform and the admin panel. Implemented fixes covering: API rate limiting on critical endpoints, secure HTTP response header configuration (Content-Security-Policy, X-Frame-Options, HSTS, X-Content-Type-Options), role-based access control enforcement for APIs and protected page routes, input sanitization for all user-submitted text fields, and JWT token security hardening. Coordinated with the external security firm and internal QA team to re-validate each fix on a staging environment before production deployment.
impact: Successfully maintained SOC Type 2 certification. All identified vulnerabilities resolved. Significantly improved platform security posture across both platforms.
learnings:
API rate limiting implementation
HTTP security header configuration (CSP, HSTS, X-Frame-Options)
Role-based access control enforcement at API and route levels
Input sanitization patterns and secure JWT handling
Coordinating security remediation with external auditors
